findings.reason: the author would generalise the existing registry and reuse the census harness instead of inventing a parallel promotion-side taxonomy, and §2's "33 of 42" would be measured against a surface already partly equipped.
findings.text: §4/§9's centrepiece (a registry giving every refusal a discharge, plus a test that enumerates the refusal sites from the source and fails on any with none) already exists for the dispatch surface: `reckon/crew/refusals.py:18` holds `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES` (D01–D23) behind `format_refusal` (`refusals.py:97`), and `tests/test_crew_refusal_visibility.py:34,66,79` AST-walks `REFUSAL_SOURCE_PATHS` and asserts each reachable family names its resolving action in the shared formatter. §9's claimed "falsifier, to be written before the change" is already written, for the dispatch surface.

findings.reason: §9's premise that §5 is "the only section that can start today" is stale; the author would either find the residual defect (the plan's own attached comment argues the positive-record form is fixture-spoofable and the fix should read declared fields, not substrings. That deeper fix is not what landed) or re-scope §5/§9.
findings.text: §5/§9's "correct test for the thing the guard is actually asking about" is already landed: `_require_gate_log_agrees` (`promotion.py:1160`) refuses the `command not found` diagnostic only when the log carries no positive record, via `_log_shows_the_command_ran` (`promotion.py:1115`), which accepts a runner result summary or a terminal `EXIT=<n>` outside `{126,127}`. The specimen log carries a real runner summary (line 663), so the third refusal no longer fires on the shape §5 describes as blocked, and `reckon/crew/promotion.py` no longer reads `recorded != 0 and re.search(...)` as §5 states.

findings.reason: the author would assert the existing capture path and name whichever lane still fails to invoke it, rather than add a parallel write; the outstanding question is a spot check of the codex dialect, not a new mechanism.
findings.text: §10's remedy ("a codex-family session records its session id into the live pointer on its first turn, exactly as the other lanes do") is already the job of `capture_run_session` (`runs.py:79`), which writes `session_id` and a `session_harness` boundary onto the run and is reached through `resolve_session` (`resumption.py:464`) across pointer, stream and ledger. The harness-boundary handling in `_current_harness_session` (`dispatch.py:11558`) and the `lane_change` record (`dispatch.py:12302`) already carry the lane-change case, and `tests/test_dispatch_reads_the_run_session.py` already asserts capture reads the stream when the pointer lags.

findings.reason: §10 should be restated as "extend `capture_run_session` so the codex dialect writes on its first turn" and §6 as reaching the existing scope-conflict claimant naming from the promotion path, which the plan's own §6 already says is "the surface exists and is simply not reached"; naming the owner would make the change an extension rather than a second reader.
findings.text: §10 (and the s10 done-write for a fresh session) forwards to session capture that `resolve_session` already performs over three sources, and §6 asks for a claimed-file owner name that `tests/test_scope_refusal_names_its_claimant.py` already asserts for scope refusals; neither section says why the existing reader cannot be extended.

rubric_items.deep_module: finding — §4 leaves the discharges' home undefined across an unresolved flag-per-refusal-vs-keyed decision, while the tree already has the one deep module for exactly this job.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 duplicates the refusal-remedy registry owned by `reckon/crew/refusals.py`, and §10 duplicates the session capture owned by `reckon/crew/runs.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: finding — the plan proposes a refusal-to-discharge registry, a source-enumerating refusal census test, a positive-evidence gate-log check and a session-capture write; none is cited, though all four already exist in the tree.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: finding — §5 and §10 each propose a layer over machinery that already exists, without arguing the machinery cannot be extended.
